Are you sure?

[quote=Spiff's Rules and Clarifications]The sotm rule book says “when a hero is reduced to 0 or fewer hp, remove all of that hero’s cards from the game, leaving only the hero character card, flipping it over so their incapacitated side is up”. this has been officially amended so that it should be read as “if a hero is destroyed, by either being reduced to 0 hp or otherwise, flip their hero character card and remove all of their cards from the game”.[/quote]emphasis mine.

 

If this is a replacement effect, the text should read "If a hero would be destroyed", or have an "instead" at the end.

 

[quote=also from Spiff's Rules and Clarifications]however, there’s a dark side to this ruling as well. the final wasteland’s “unforgiving wasteland” card says that whenever a target would be destroyed by damage dealt by an environment card, remove that target from the game instead”. this means that if a hero is destroyed when “unforgiving wasteland” is in play, it will be removed from the game entirely rather than flipping to its incapacitated side and remaining in the game.[/quote]

This sounds to me like heroes do get destroyed - they simply are affected differently by destruction.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Character cards can be destroyed.  Wrathful Gaze does not flip Spite, it destroyes him, and if it flipped Apostate it wouldn't be awesome.  But it is awesome, because character cards can be destroyed.  It's why Shrine says that when an ennead is destroyed it flips, and why Talisman says it is indestructible and has text explaining what to do with it when it is destroyed.

 

I don't see why the character card would not go under La Capitan.

I understand that they are removed instead of incapped because of the "would be" in unforgiving wasteland.

If a character card is destroyed you flip it, remove all other cards from the game.

The Character card is still there.  It is in play, it is still the same hero card, it has been destroyed by a villain card.  By other ruling we know that it hasn't left play or entered play.  It is still the same card.

It still meets all the qualifications to go under La Capitan.

There is no ruling that puts an "would be" or "instead" into the incap text, and nothing says Character cards can't be destroyed.

Does Skydeck put the card into the trash and then under the deck?

No.

The text affecting what happens to it when it is destroyed replaces the normal effect of being destroyed.  Not the destruction, unless it states "when it would be destroyed . . . instead."  then it is replacing the destruction.

The hero character card destruction special rules replace teh normal effect of being destroyed, not the destruction itself.

So the hero character card does not go to the trash, it flips and remains in play, because the special rules for hero character cards replaces that normal effect.  Also I don't think an Incapped hero has a trash, without a deck or cards why would it?  All it has left is a character card.

Here we have a situation with a rule that still has room to perform its effect.  The special rules for Hero character card destruction can take place, and the effect of La Capitan putting the card under her card can still take place afterward.

Whether that is what officially should happen is unknown, but the rulings we have leave the door open for it, and no ruling we have says it cannot happen.
